content: Goal: choose a shallow-only curvature mechanism that couples training-only directed transitions to the level-1 RQ-VAE assignment while leaving levels >=2 exactly baseline. Read: workspace contains only progress.jsonl; no repository files were available, so the design uses the frozen-scale facts and the four previous arm results given in the task. Observed: prior rejections show deep-layer crowding survives even with per-layer curvature and Sinkhorn, so the new candidate must not touch deep assignment and must not use transport/Sinkhorn. Reasoning: propose SGSA-RQ, a first-level Poincare successor anchor. Training-only directed transition counts define a top-M successor set per item; its weighted Frechet mean in the Poincare ball is a behavior anchor. The level-1 score subtracts both the curved item-to-code distance and the curved anchor-to-code distance, so behavior changes the hard code choice and therefore the residual seen by every baseline deep layer. Deep layers remain Euclidean argmin with no behavior term. Open: final JSON must carry all requested fields, three switches, derived constants, and frozen-scale cost.

Final answer record for SGSA-RQ. The candidate is a shallow-only curvature mechanism: a training-only directed-transition successor set defines a weighted Frechet anchor in the Poincare ball, and only the level-1 RQ score uses that anchor plus the curved item-code distance. Levels 2..L are exactly baseline Euclidean residual quantization with argmin, no behavior, no Sinkhorn. Three switches exist in code: behavior off sets a_i=u_i; geometry off replaces the Poincare map/distance/Frechet mean with Euclidean identity/weighted mean; both on is the full coupled run. Constants: fixed curvature -1, top-M=8 successors, 3 Frechet iterations, scale s measured once at initialization, normalizers D_item and D_anchor measured once, no sweep. Frozen-scale cost is confined to level 1 and an epoch-end anchor refresh; deep levels are bit-identical baseline. The complete JSON answer follows in the final response and is also the requested answer block.

Euclidean level-1 clustering ignores training-only directed transitions, so items that frequently precede the same successors are not deliberately placed near a behaviorally meaningful shallow region. The later levels must keep the baseline dispersion that the previous deep-curvature arms lost.","novelty":"This is a single fixed-curvature Poincare layer, not a per-layer curvature field, not capacity cells, not per-occupant reach radii, and not Sinkhorn/transport. A training-only successor set is summarized as a weighted Poincare Frechet anchor, and that anchor gates only the level-1 hard code choice; levels 2..L are exactly the baseline Euclidean residual quantizer. No extra behavior loss and no code reassignment at deep levels are introduced.","key_change":"Only the level-1 RQ assignment changes. Its score subtracts a normalized Poincare item-to-code distance and a normalized Poincare anchor-to-code distance. The selected level-1 code fixes the Euclidean residual passed to levels 2..L, which remain byte-identical baseline argmin Euclidean residual quantization.","specification":"Build a directed transition table only from Stage2 training sequences. For each item i keep top-M=8 successors S_i with row-normalized weights p(j|i). Map encoder outputs h_i and level-1 code vectors e_1k into the curvature -1 Poincare ball with phi. Compute a weighted Poincare Frechet mean a_i of the successor embeddings. Level-1 score is s_ik = -d_P(phi(h_i),phi(e_1k))/D_item - d_P(phi(e_1k),a_i)/D_anchor; choose k_i1=argmin_k s_ik; use q_i1=e_1,k_i1 and r_i=h_i-q_i1; then run baseline Euclidean RQ for l=2..L. D_item and D_anchor are single training-set medians measured at initialization and frozen; no sweep and no ablation run.","cost_estimate":"Extra compute is confined to level 1 and an epoch-end anchor refresh. At the frozen scale of 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch and 3000 epochs, with K1=256 level-1 codes, the added Poincare distance work is about 24556*256 = 6.29M distance evaluations per epoch, about 262k per step. The anchor refresh is about 24556*8*3 = 589k log/exp operations per epoch, about 24.6k per step amortized. Deep levels are bit-identical baseline. Estimated +5 to +8 percent training wall-clock and about +0.2 GB for the anchor table; no extra full forward pass is needed because h_i are cached during the epoch.","falsifiable_hypothesis":"If the shallow successor anchor is the right coupling, one run should give valid level-1 hard ER at most 4 and positive hit rate at least 0.12, while level2 distinct prefixes stay at or above the baseline order of 7414, l3_collision stays at most 0.35, and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065. If level-1 separation improves but Stage3 recall remains at or below 0.065, or if l3_collision rises above 0.35, the anchor is not useful.","risks":["The successor Frechet anchor may pull many items toward popular successor means and reduce level-1 separation, raising hard ER above 4.","Sparse or noisy directed transitions may make a_i uninformative or unstable for long-tail items.","The scale normalizers D_item and D_anchor measured once at initialization may drift as the encoder changes.","Hard argmin gives no dir

Row-normalize p(j|i)=C_ij/sum_m C_im and keep the top M=8 successors S_i by p. Build the anchor from S_i and p(j|i) only. Encoder training uses the training split; validation is only a recorded diagnostic.","hyperbolic_operator":"Fixed negative curvature c=-1 Poincare ball. Removing behavior sets a_i=u_i and changes k_i1; replacing d_P by Euclidean changes k_i1.","coupling_equation":"s_ik = - d_P(phi(h_i), phi(e_1k)) / D_item - d_P(phi(e_1k), a_i) / D_anchor, with a_i = Frechet_P({phi(h_j)}_{j in S_i}, {p(j|i)}), and k_i1 = argmin_k s_ik.","observables":"Valid level-1 hard ER, level-1 positive hit rate, level2 distinct prefixes, l3_collision, and Stage3 test_recall@10. D_item=median_i d_P(u_i,c_{k_iE}) at init, D_anchor=median over nonempty S_i of d_P(c_{k_iE},a_i) at init, where k_iE is the Euclidean level-1 argmin at init. At the end of each epoch cache h_i for all training items and refresh a_i for the next epoch with stop-gradient.","spec_inputs_outputs":"Inputs: batch encoder outputs h_i, level-1 and deep codebooks e_lk, training-only successor table S_i and p(j|i), current anchor table a_i, scale s, and frozen normalizers D_item and D_anchor. Outputs: discrete level-1 index k_i1, Euclidean quantized vector q_i1 used by the decoder, residuals r_i for levels 2..L, baseline deep indices k_il, and the standard RQ-VAE reconstruction and codebook gradients.","safeguards":"Use float32 for arcosh, log and exp. Clamp ||a|| and ||b|| to at most 1-1e-7 before d_P. Clamp the arcosh argument to at least 1+1e-12. Normalize successor weights and skip empty S_i by setting a_i=u_i and excluding that item from the D_anchor median. Detach a_i and successor embeddings so the anchor cannot backpropagate through other items. Fix curvature -1, M=8, Frechet iterations=3, and the scale s measured once at initialization; do not sweep them. Assert that every level l>=2 uses Euclidean cdist and argmin and contains no behavior term. Do not use Sinkhorn or any transport balancing. At SID construction for validation and test items, use only the frozen training-derived codebook and no test-time transitions."}
